checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Four separate square slides, exact names, in order
must.why: Four square images in the order Monstera, Snake plant, Pothos, Peace lily. Names are in all caps, which is a stylistic choice.
The monstera has split leaves, the snake plant has upright leaves, and the pothos has trailing vines. The peace lily has white spathes, though they are small and outlined rather than solid white.
All four use the same green on cream with a linocut look.

must.item: Border, lettering, texture and pot consistent
must.why: The border, corner leaves, serif font, paper and banded pot look identical. Only tiny differences exist, such as the pot's rim in the pothos slide being partly hidden by leaves.

must.item: Only plant and name change; layout aligned; names readable
must.why: The layout is aligned and the names are clear. The pothos vines overlap the pot slightly, which is natural.

faults.what: The peace lily spathes are pale outlined shapes, not strongly white, so they read only weakly as flowers.
The names are in all caps, whereas the user wrote them in sentence case.
The images are low resolution (640px) and a little soft.

summary: Four highly consistent sage-and-cream linocut slides with the same border, lettering, texture and pot, and clearly distinct plants. The only weak spot is the faint peace lily spathe.
